changesSinceHistoricalCorpus.jsLibScopeSealing: 14dd2494 sealed the shared scope, so ScriptableObject.putImpl refused a write with msg.modify.sealed; a7d37f1707a70a459ad708f4fe79341d1e42d716 replaces sealing with globalThis.preventExtensions() plus a per-source shared global object keyed by MD5(jsLib):sourceClass:MD5(sourceKey) (BaseSourceExtensions.kt:17-21, ScriptBindings.kt:32-46,115-127). A write to an existing jsLib top-level binding is therefore no longer refused by sealing; the corpus never performs one, so no compared row changes.
changesSinceHistoricalCorpus.analyzeUrlConstructor: the selected AnalyzeUrl declares sixteen constructor parameters, the historical fourteen plus nullable infoMap and extraParams (AnalyzeUrl.kt:83-98); the harness resolves the declaration and records the arity it used.
changesSinceHistoricalCorpus.evalJSEntryPoint: AnalyzeUrl.evalJS(jsStr, result) keeps its two parameters (AnalyzeUrl.kt:395).

sharedTopLevelWrite.note: At a7d37f1707a70a459ad708f4fe79341d1e42d716 the library scope is made non-extensible with globalThis.preventExtensions() and each evaluation chains fresh bindings whose globalThis.prototype is that scope or the per-source shared global derived from it; top-level declarations stay in the per-evaluation scope. Whether a library function that assigns a jsLib top-level binding succeeds, silently fails or throws is therefore not asserted here: the corpus mutates only the shared object's property (sharedState.n), and the question is reported, not compared and not repaired in product code.
